item.title: A small app, two app stores, fourteen days
item.description:
Tour of the Bible has a mobile app now. iOS is on the App Store. Android is in closed testing on Google Play, walking out the 14-day clock that Google now imposes on every new developer account before they let you near the production track. The same JavaScript bundle drives both apps and the website it grew out of.

I expected this to be straightforward. The reading-plan logic, the verse fetcher, the lexicon, the audio player — all of that already existed in the web version. I told myself I was wrapping it for a phone.

item.title: Building Tour of the Bible: A 66-Book Reading Companion with No Backend
item.description:
Why I built it

Matt Whitman — the “Ten Minute Bible Hour” guy — wrote a short piece called the Lightning-Fast Field Guide to the Bible: 66 books, roughly 90 minutes, a couple of key passages per book to give you the taste without the full commitment. I loved the idea. I wanted a cleaner way to work through it than a physical checklist and a notes app, with the passages right there to tap on rather than switching to a Bible app and losing my place.
